note: Version 2 adds the tokens the Companion, Trust and App Capsule surfaces need. Nothing in version 1 changed value: an existing surface renders identically, and the additions are named for the decision they carry rather than for how they look, so a high-contrast or reduced-transparency theme can redefine them without a surface knowing.

flat.note: Content that sits in the page.

modal.note: The Trust prompt, which is the only modal Bunny raises unasked.

focus.note: A visible ring on every focusable control in every theme. Never removed for aesthetics; a keyboard-only session is a supported way to use Bunny OS and an invisible focus makes it a guessing game.

scrim.note: solid is used at high contrast, where a light dim leaves a modal indistinguishable from the page behind it.

companion.note: One entry per companion.presentation phase, so a phase the runtime can produce always has something to draw. 'attention' intensity is the only one that may pulse, and only when the motion budget is non-zero.

risk.note: A marker is a shape beside the heading, not only a colour: colour alone fails for a person who cannot distinguish these hues, and a permission prompt is the worst place for that failure.

standing.note: unenforced is a state a permission row can be in *as well as* granted, and it is drawn as a badge rather than replacing the standing, because 'allowed and not actually restricted' is two facts.

opacity.note: Reduced-transparency mode makes every surface opaque rather than merely less transparent; a translucent panel over a busy wallpaper is the case that motivates the setting.

contrast.note: WCAG 2.2 AA. Checked by tests/accessibility against the two palettes and the high-contrast theme rather than asserted here.
